runtime_flags_note: --max-model-len/--max-num-seqs/--max-num-batched-tokens were reduced from the model's own officially documented values (262144/128/16384) since this is a trivial compatibility smoke, not a production capacity test. --tensor-parallel-size 2 and --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA were kept identical to the model's own documented launch command (evidence-based topology, not inflated or under-provisioned).
topology_calculation: Published weight footprint: 117,879,865,344 FP8 params (~117.9GB at 1 byte/param) + 1,521,452,032 BF16 params (~3.0GB at 2 bytes/param) = ~120.9GB total, per the repository's own model.safetensors.index.json (total_size=120922770560 bytes). A single H200 (141GB) would leave only ~20GB headroom for CUDA context, KV cache, and vLLM's own profiling/graph-capture overhead -- the model's own officially documented vLLM launch command specifies --tensor-parallel-size 2, which was adopted directly as the evidence-based topology rather than guessed.
vram_measurement_limitation: peak_allocated_vram_gb/peak_reserved_vram_gb in the manifest reflect only the Modal Function's own (API-server) process CUDA context, which is 0.0 on both GPUs -- vLLM's tensor-parallel executor spawns separate OS worker subprocesses (Worker_TP0, Worker_TP1) that hold the actual GPU memory allocations for the loaded weights, and those subprocess-level CUDA statistics were not captured by the parent process before the crash. This is an honest measurement gap, not a fabricated zero: real GPU memory was allocated (weight load succeeded in attempt 2 before the profiling-stage crash), but its magnitude was not observed by any process this smoke queried.
